title: Make Invalid Rows Impossible
concept: Enforce domain invariants in a real database

writing.summary: Enforce domain invariants in a real database.
writing.rule: Validate in Rust for helpful errors and in SQL for every writer.
writing.explanation:
Task Ledger must not accept empty titles just because a caller bypasses the API. A database schema is an independent enforcement boundary. Give each task an integer primary key, require a title whose trimmed length is between 1 and 80, and constrain done to exactly 0 or 1 with a default of 0.

A CHECK returning null can behave differently from a false expression; NOT NULL remains a separate requirement. A default applies when a column is omitted, not when a caller explicitly sends null. SQLite trim without a second argument removes ordinary spaces, rather than Rust's full Unicode whitespace set. Store canonical titles and keep that policy explicit. Migration history belongs in version control. Once a production schema exists, changing CREATE TABLE text does not update an existing database: write and test a migration. This lab starts from a fresh SQLite database and executes your DDL, then tries valid, null, empty, duplicate and out-of-domain writes. It does not merely compare the SQL text.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Run sqlite3 tasks.db .read migrations/001.sql, then attempt valid and invalid INSERT statements. The compiler lab executes your DDL against fresh real SQLite.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: This Rust reading prints a SQL statement. The independent compiler lab executes it against real SQLite.
writing.task: Return DDL creating tasks(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,title TEXT NOT NULL,done INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0). Enforce a trimmed title length of 1..=80 and done IN (0,1) using SQL constraints. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: Why keep SQL constraints when the Rust handler already validates titles?
answers: Other writers and future bugs can bypass the handler
A Rust validation function automatically changes the database schema
writing.feedback: The database must protect its own invariant independently of one application entry point.
